newsitem.title: USA: Herman briefs Clinton on UPS strike.
newsitem.headline: Herman briefs Clinton on UPS strike.

text.p: Labour Secretary Alexis Herman briefed President Clinton on the United Parcel Service strike Tuesday, telling reporters afterward that she was somewhat encouraged about the prospects for resolving the dispute.
"I'm encouraged in that I believe that both sides expressed a willingness to be more flexible in looking at their own differences," Herman told reporters travelling with Clinton to St. Louis.

Herman met separately with UPS and Teamsters union officials on Monday in an effort to get them back to the bargaining table to seek an end to the nine-day strike, which has crippled the Atlanta-based parcel delivery company.

"They both recognise that there is much at stake for the workers, for the company and for the American people," Herman said. "When you put it all together I have to believe that there is more of a willingness to at least to seek some kind of a resolution between the two parties."

Clinton, in St. Louis to make a speech about moving people from welfare to work, has so far refused to intervene in the strike, saying it has not yet reached the required standard of imperilling the national health or economy.
Herman, who briefed Clinton as they flew to St. Louis on Air Force One, suggested this was still his position.
"We continue to monitor this situation on a daily basis and I don't believe that it constitutes a national emergency at this time," she said.
Herman also said she expected to hear from both parties either late on Tuesday or early on Wednesday.
UPS and Teamsters union representatives met Herman Monday but there were no signs of a break in the 9-day-old strike.
Teamsters President Ron Carey told reporters after his meeting with the labour secretary that he was ready to go back to the bargaining table, but only for serious negotiations.

UPS negotiator Dave Murray said the firm was not changing its offer despite Herman's calls for flexibility. "We still believe that the correct solution to this is for the Teamsters to put our people back to work and send our offer out for a vote," Murray said.
